decisions.question: How is a task’s status stored so both artifacts update automatically?

options.label: One registry
options.summary: Each status stored once, as a task registry inside the full-progress artifact. One command regenerates the feature artifact's and full-progress artifact's checklists from it. Cannot drift.

options.label: Write both, then sync
options.summary: Status written on the feature artifact and the full-progress artifact separately; a sync step compares them and flags disagreements. Closer to the original proposal; can still drift between syncs.

decisions.question: Do branch names start with the task ID?

options.label: Yes, task ID first
options.summary: Hooks match git/gh events to tasks automatically and queue the status change.

options.label: No convention
options.summary: Branches stay free-form; hooks can only remind the session to update statuses, not say which task changed.

decisions.question: How do changes made outside a session reach the artifacts?

options.label: Next session start
options.summary: A session-start hook checks GitHub and queues the changes. No extra cost; artifacts can lag until the next session.

options.label: Also a cloud routine
options.summary: A scheduled cloud agent also checks and updates artifacts when no session is open. Always current; costs a recurring run.

decisions.question: What look do artifacts get?

options.label: Neutral, comic optional
options.summary: A plain neutral theme by default; the current comic look ships as a theme a project can choose.

options.label: Comic for every project
options.summary: The comic look from another project becomes the default everywhere.

options.label: Each project’s own design, else a default
options.summary: Look and feel taken from the project it belongs to (scan its design files or web pages); a project with no design gets a default design file shipped in the plugin. The other project’s comic look is ignored.

decisions.chosen: Each project’s own design, else a default
decisions.owner_words: ignore the [another project] look; all artificts should have a look & feel based on the project they belong too ([…]); if project has no design, then put together a default design file in this plugin; and since dev-standards proejct has no design since its just for plugins, the create the default design and its file now, and apply it to existing artifacts

decisions.question: An App / service column on the full-progress artifact?

options.label: Yes, full-progress only
options.summary: It covers every app and service, so you can scan one area. Feature artifacts keep four columns.

options.label: No, four columns everywhere
options.summary: Same columns on every artifact; the app or service goes in the Detail text.

decisions.question: Where is the record kept?

options.label: Dedicated branch
options.summary: An orphan branch, e.g. project-artifacts, holding only the record. Updates commit there without a checkout, so code branches, PRs and CI never see them and parallel agents can't conflict with them.

options.label: Folder on the default branch
options.summary: .claude/project-artifacts/ on main. Easy to find, but every status change is a commit to main: CI has to skip those paths, and it bends the 'nothing lands on main one change at a time' rule.

options.label: Folder on each work branch
options.summary: The status change rides the branch doing the work and reaches main with its PR. The record on main lags, and parallel branches conflict on the registry.

options.label: The repo’s docs/artifacts folder
options.summary: The record (manifest, registry, content, last published HTML) lives in docs/artifacts/ on the repo, and every doc goes under docs/.

decisions.owner_words: on the repos docs/artifacts folder; the project-setup plugin should set a more general rule for all docs to be created in the docs/ folder;

decisions.question: How does a project get the plugin?

options.label: project-setup installs it
options.summary: Every project set up by luismc-project-setup gets it, and no artifact is created until the first feature artifact is made.

options.label: Opt-in per project
options.summary: You install it yourself in the projects that want it.

options.label: Project-setup installs it, plus independent install
options.summary: Every project set up by luismc-project-setup gets it, and any project can also install it on its own. No artifact is created until the first feature artifact is made.

decisions.chosen: Project-setup installs it, plus independent install
decisions.owner_words: option 1 plus the ability to install independently per project

decisions.question: Which clock do Expected times use?

options.label: Owner's zone, per project
options.summary: Set once in each project's manifest; Lisbon for your projects. The zone is named in the column header.

options.label: Always Lisbon
options.summary: Fixed for every project.

options.label: UTC
options.summary: The same everywhere, but you would have to convert it in your head.

decisions.question: Does dev-standards move other projects onto the plugin?

options.label: Branch and draft PR
options.summary: Push a task-ID branch with a draft PR. You review it and merge it yourself.

options.label: Merge on green there too
options.summary: Same flow as here: one ready PR, merged on green.

options.label: Local only
options.summary: Prepare the change in a local clone and push nothing. Leave a report for you.

options.label: Leave other projects alone
options.summary: dev-standards ships the plugin and names or changes no other project; each project adopts it in its own sessions.

decisions.owner_words: why are you touch another project?

decisions.question: Full Progress: release timeline above the status table and a State column in the feature table (preview, Version 70); adopt for the plugin?

options.label: As previewed
options.summary: Phases sized from the basis, hatched margin up to Expected.

options.label: With the two changes
options.summary: Expected = the sum of the phases (no silent padding); risk drawn as a named faint extension (e.g. +1 fix round ~10 min) ending at an outlined worst-case marker, only when the basis names it.

options.label: Change something else
options.summary: Owner names other changes.

decisions.owner_words: For the plugin version add the two things; also apply now to full progress page

decisions.question: How does a release get its RELEASE-<n> number?

options.label: Number on the release task
options.summary: The release stays a task (its ID still starts branch names); --release gives it the next project-wide number, never reused, shown as RELEASE-12.

options.label: Release is its own entity
options.summary: RELEASE-12 is a separate record, not a task; join, CI and merge are ordinary tasks that point at it.

decisions.owner_words: releases should be numbered with "RELEASE-<release number>"

decisions.question: How does Full Progress show which items go into each release?

options.label: Group rows by release
options.summary: One group per open release in Expected order with the release row and every item riding it, then Not in a release yet, then the other groups.

options.label: Release column
options.summary: Keep today's groups and add a Release column with a RELEASE-n chip on each row.

options.label: Both
options.summary: Group by release and also show a Release chip on each row.

decisions.owner_words: its hard to know what items go into each release

decisions.question: Must items be assigned to a release?

options.label: Built must name one
options.summary: A Built task must ride a release; other statuses may stay unassigned; Live rows keep their release.

options.label: Every open item
options.summary: Running, To do, Waiting, Built and the rest all must ride a release.

options.label: Optional
options.summary: Never required; unassigned items show as Not in a release yet.

options.label: Built and Running must name one
options.summary: Owner's variant: the first option, with Running tasks required to ride a release too.

decisions.chosen: Built and Running must name one

decisions.question: Should the status tiles say they count tasks?

options.label: Relabel
options.summary: Tile labels read 'tasks live', 'tasks built' and so on, so 123 is not read as releases.

options.label: Keep the labels
options.summary: Tiles keep the bare status word.

decisions.owner_words: relabel; ensure all the changes are part of the artifacts plugin so other projects use it

decisions.question: How is Running work that ships nothing (a publish, a study, a cleanup) handled under the rule that Running and Built ride a release?

options.label: Mark it 'ships nothing'
options.summary: An explicit no-release flag with a reason lets a task be Running without a release; Built still always rides one.

options.label: Only Built must ride
options.summary: Running may be unassigned; Built must ride a release.

options.label: Keep it strict
options.summary: Every Running task rides a release, chores included.
